instruction: Single Room IFC Shell This task starts from scratch with no init_file inputs and no local reference images. Create a metric IFC4 single-room BIM shell and save the required output as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc. 1. The output folder contains /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc, and /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc is at least 500 bytes. 2. /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc uses an IFC4 schema. 3. The IFC model contains exactly 1 IfcProject, 1 IfcSite, 1 IfcBuilding, 1 IfcBuildingStorey, 1 IfcSpace, 4 IfcWall entities, 1 IfcSlab, 1 IfcDoor, 1 IfcWindow, 2 IfcOpeningElement entities, 2 IfcRelVoidsElement relationships, and 2 IfcRelFillsElement relationships. 4. The IFC model contains 0 IfcBuildingElementProxy, 0 IfcFurniture, 0 IfcRoof, 0 IfcColumn, 0 IfcBeam, 0 IfcStair, and 0 IfcFlowTerminal entities. 5. All IfcRoot GlobalId values are unique. 6. The single IfcSpace is named exactly Room 101, ignoring leading and trailing whitespace only. 7. The single IfcSpace, all 4 walls, the slab, the door, and the window are spatially assigned to the single IfcBuildingStorey. 8. The IfcSpace geometry has clear plan dimensions 6.00 m by 4.00 m, in either X/Y orientation, with tolerance +/-0.05 m. 9. Each wall has height 3.00 m with tolerance +/-0.05 m and thickness 0.20 m with tolerance +/-0.03 m. 10. The slab has thickness 0.20 m with tolerance +/-0.05 m. 11. The door OverallWidth is 0.90 m with tolerance +/-0.05 m and the door fills exactly one IfcOpeningElement that voids an IfcWall. 12. The window OverallWidth is 1.50 m with tolerance +/-0.05 m and the window fills exactly one different IfcOpeningElement that voids an IfcWall. 13. The door opening is hosted by the south wall, defined as the wall with the lowest world-coordinate center Y value. 14. The window opening is hosted by the east wall, defined as the wall with the highest world-coordinate center X value. Any item not explicitly required may vary.
